svg.text: BEST FOR: WHERE AGENTS WORK TODAY
FORMAT LINEAGE: Ethan Mollick, jagged frontier (Dell'Acqua et al. 2023)
Where Agents Work Today — a Jagged Frontier Map You Can Redraw Every Month
Ethan Mollick's framing from the Harvard/BCG field experiment: AI capability is not a smooth wall; it is jagged. Tasks that look similar sit on opposite sides.
agents succeed reliably today — delegate these
looks doable, fails unpredictably — keep a human in the loop
Task placement is an engineering judgment for coding/support agents in 2026 — redraw it with your own 20-task sample.
THE STUDY BEHIND THE IDEA (DELL'ACQUA ET AL., 2023 — 758 BCG CONSULTANTS)
more tasks completed by consultants using GPT-4 inside
less likely to produce correct solutions on the task
HOW TO DRAW YOUR OWN FRONTIER (MONTHLY, 1 HOUR)
Pick 20 real tasks your team gives the agent; run each 3 times.
Automate inside tasks fully; keep humans on the edge; do not
Repeat monthly — model upgrades move the edge, but never
Model releases, better tools (code execution, retrieval), and
tighter harnesses (tests, checkpoints) each push specific bumps of
the frontier outward — which is why a task that failed in March
can pass in June while its neighbor still fails.
Never assume a task is inside the frontier because a similar one is — check it.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
